typically calculated using a computer program. A more accu-
rate method for determining adequacy of HD is the eKt/V, in 
which e stands for equilibrated and takes into account the 
amount of time it takes for urea to equilibrate across cell mem-
branes after dialysis has stopped. An acceptable eKt/V is 1.2 or 
greater.
Another method to determine effective dialysis treatment is 
the urea reduction ratio (URR), which looks at the reduction 
in urea before and after dialysis. The patient is considered well 
dialyzed when a 65% or greater reduction in the serum urea 
occurs during dialysis. Unlike Kt/V, this calculation can be 
done quickly at the patient’s bedside by the practitioner. The
